title: quercus brachyphylla subsp. tommasinii
intro: Quercus brachyphylla subsp. tommasinii, commonly known as the Dinaric white oak, is a subspecies of evergreen tree native to the Dinaric Alps in the Balkans. This plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine to treat various health conditions, with its leaves and bark offering potential health benefits such as reducing inflammation and improving cardiovascular health. The therapeutic actions of Quercus brachyphylla subsp. tommasinii include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids. The bioactive constituents of this plant have been shown to possess anti-cancer and neuroprotective effects, highlighting its potential as a valuable medicinal resource.
